items.text: While alive supervision is active, when a supervised task has not completed an execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own, the supervisor shall detect an alive fault with fault code 1.
The supervisor shall start alive supervision when the start-up integrity checks have passed.

When a supervised task starts later than the late-start limit of that task, counted from the release of that task, the supervisor shall detect a late-start fault with fault code 2, and a start at or before the limit is accepted.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r1-006. CON-SUP-103 defines a late start as a start later than the limit and does not state the instant of detection; CON-SUP-105 does not name late start at the limit. The requirement no longer mandates detection at the expiry instant. The detection instant for a task that has not started at all is recorded in OP-SYS-010 and the coincident 100 µs step in OP-SYS-009 (both deferred to sw-req); a task that never starts is also covered by alive supervision (SYS-SUP-001).

items.text: When a supervised task has not completed its execution at the instant the execution limit of that task expires, counted from the start of that execution, the supervisor shall detect an overrun fault with fault code 3 at that instant, without waiting for the task to complete, and a completion at or before the expiry of the limit is accepted.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-002. CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the limit expires, and CON-SUP-105 makes the expiry of a timing limit the instant the fault becomes detectable. The requirement now ties detection to the expiry instant itself instead of to a later measurement step. An execution longer than the limit is an overrun and an execution not longer than the limit is not, so a completion at or before expiry is accepted (CON-SUP-103). How a completion that coincides with the expiry within the 100 µs resolution of SYS-SUP-008 is resolved is a measurement detail left open in OP-SYS-009. SYS-SUP-003 states the late-start rule separately and is not changed here.

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle have not arrived in the configured order or a checkpoint is missing, the supervisor shall detect a flow fault with fault code 4.

The supervisor shall read the set of supervised tasks, their periods, late-start limits, execution limits and checkpoint order from the configuration data, so that changing them requires no change to the supervisor code.

The supervisor shall supervise three 10 ms tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, released in that order every 10 ms, and the 100 ms task T_DIAG, released after T_OUT in every tenth 10 ms period, with default limits of a late start after 2 ms, an execution longer than 3 ms for each 10 ms task and an execution longer than 20 ms for T_DIAG.
The supervisor shall measure task start delays and execution times with a resolution of 100 µs.

When the configuration data at start-up contains a timing limit longer than the period of its task, a task period of zero, or an entry naming an unknown task (CON-SUP-115), the supervisor shall detect a configuration fault with fault code 9.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-003. Detection is kept here; the safe-state latch on fault code 9 is split into SYS-SUP-043 so each can be verified independently. Other items that cite SYS-SUP-009 for the latch (SYS-SUP-013, SYS-SUP-021, SYS-SUP-027, SYS-SUP-042) now find it in SYS-SUP-043.

items.text: When the independent watchdog, which runs from its own clock, has not been serviced for 100 ms, the controller shall perform a reset.

At the end of each control cycle, when no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall refresh the window watchdog once.
items.rationale: Reworked for F-sys-req-item-r2-004. The refresh condition is now the exact complement of the withholding condition in SYS-SUP-013: SYS-SUP-013 withholds every watchdog service action from the detection of a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 until the next reset and while the safe state is latched, so a cycle with no new detection that follows an earlier detection, or that occurs while the safe state is latched, gets no refresh. Both requirements use the same fault-code set, so they never demand opposite actions; the resulting missing refresh is handled by SYS-SUP-012 and SYS-SUP-010.

items.text: When the window watchdog is refreshed earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh, the controller shall perform a reset.

From the instant a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 is detected until the next reset, and at all times while the safe state is latched, the supervisor shall withhold every watchdog service action, including the refresh of the window watchdog.
items.rationale: STK-SUP-005 allows servicing only while every supervised task is healthy; a supervised task is healthy while no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 is detected. Withholding starts at the detection instant, which CON-SUP-105 defines per fault class, and persists after detection (it does not end when the fault condition disappears) until a reset ends the safe-state reaction of CON-SUP-110; a latched safe state (SYS-SUP-009, SYS-SUP-028) keeps the supervisor unhealthy, so withholding continues. Fault code 8 is reported after a reset and is not a health condition of a running task. The resulting missing refresh ends in a reset through SYS-SUP-012 and SYS-SUP-010. Interaction with the latched safe state (F-sys-req-set-r2-011): while the latch is set, the withholding forces watchdog resets, and the outputs are held in the safe state through each of them by SYS-SUP-046; the latch survives those resets (SYS-SUP-029) and ends only at a power-on reset (SYS-SUP-045).

items.text: Before releasing any task, the supervisor shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up with fault code 5 when the program code between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end does not match its stored reference.

Before releasing any task, the supervisor shall detect a configuration integrity fault with fault code 6 when the CRC-32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7) computed over the configuration data block differs from the CRC-32 stored with that block.
While the application runs, the supervisor shall check one 1 KiB segment of the program code in each control cycle.
The supervisor shall complete a full pass of the run-time program-code check of a 1 MiB image within 11 s.
The supervisor shall use at most 0.5 ms of processor time per control cycle for the run-time program-code check.
When the run-time program-code check finds a mismatch with the stored reference, the supervisor shall detect a run-time code integrity fault with fault code 7.
From any reset until the start-up integrity checks have passed, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low.

While the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall drive the status signal high.
items.rationale: Passing the start-up checks is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the high (operational) level of CON-SUP-109. A detected fault (SYS-SUP-022) or a latched safe state (SYS-SUP-009, SYS-SUP-028) takes precedence and keeps the status signal low until a power-on reset, so this requirement cannot override the latch. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-013: the condition now uses the same since-the-last-reset wording as SYS-SUP-011, SYS-SUP-013 and SYS-SUP-044, so a fault that clears before the reset does not raise the status signal again. The status signal is low from the detection (SYS-SUP-022) until the next reset; after that reset SYS-SUP-020 holds it low until the start-up checks have passed, and only then, if the safe state is not latched, does this item raise it, which matches the recovery sequence of STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 is detected, the controller shall drive both control outputs low and the status signal low within 50 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
items.rationale: The detectable instant is defined in CON-SUP-105 per fault class.

items.text: The supervisor shall send the fault report on the diagnostic serial line within 10 ms of the detection of the fault.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-112 fixes the 10 ms deadline from detection; CON-SUP-110 says the report is transmitted after entering the safe state; SYS-SUP-022 allows up to 50 ms for safe-state entry. Both orders cannot hold with a 50 ms entry time: transmission after entry within 10 ms of detection would force entry within 10 ms. The author does not choose between the order, the 10 ms deadline and the 50 ms entry time; see OP-SYS-008. This item states only the 10 ms deadline from detection, which is verifiable as written, and takes no position on the order relative to safe-state entry.

items.text: The supervisor shall send each fault report as the text line FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed.

The supervisor shall assign fault codes as follows: 1 alive, 2 late start, 3 overrun, 4 flow, 5 code integrity at start-up, 6 configuration integrity, 7 code integrity at run time, 8 watchdog reset, 9 configuration out of range.
The supervisor shall report the task name as entity for fault codes 1 to 4, the entity CODE for fault codes 5 and 7, and the entity CONFIG for fault code 6.

When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall request a software reset after the fault report has been transmitted and within 20 ms of entering the safe state.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-110 does not name the start of the 20 ms; entry into the safe state is taken as the reference. The reset request applies only to a safe state that is not latched: a configuration fault (fault code 9) latches the safe state until a power-on reset (SYS-SUP-009, CON-SUP-115) and a repeated fault latches it as in SYS-SUP-028 (CON-SUP-110), so no reset is requested there (SYS-SUP-042). Fault code 8 is reported after a reset and does not enter the safe state. Whether the latch of SYS-SUP-028 is in effect at the third detection or after the third reset is open in OP-SYS-001; the order of report and entry is open in OP-SYS-008.

items.text: When three consecutive supervisor resets with the same fault code have occurred without 60 s of fault-free operation in between, the controller shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
The supervisor shall keep the safe-state latch and the fault history in memory that survives software resets and watchdog resets.
At start-up, the supervisor shall classify the reset cause from the reset flags as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor reset or other.
At start-up, the supervisor shall send the classified reset cause in a start-up message on the diagnostic serial line.
When the classified reset cause is independent watchdog or window watchdog, the supervisor shall send a fault report with fault code 8.
When the request GET STATUS is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall return STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms.
When the request GET FAULTS is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall return the last 8 fault reports within 50 ms.
When any other request is received on the diagnostic serial line, the supervisor shall answer ERR.
The supervisor shall use the diagnostic serial line at 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

The supervisor shall use no more than 10 % of the processor time, measured as its execution time over any 1 s window in normal operation without fault and without service request on the simulator at the configured core clock.
The supervisor test build shall provide a test hook that injects each fault class with fault codes 1 to 9.
The supervisor shall exclude the fault-injection test hooks from the production build.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-116 states the hooks exist only in test builds.

items.text: The supervisor shall run on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board.
The supervisor shall use no dynamic memory allocation and no recursion.
While the safe state is latched, the supervisor shall not request a software reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-027 to resolve its conflict with SYS-SUP-009 and SYS-SUP-028, which latch the safe state until a power-on reset. The point at which the repeated-fault latch takes effect is open in OP-SYS-001.

items.text: When a configuration fault with fault code 9 is detected, the controller shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-009 (F-sys-req-item-r2-003). The detection of fault code 9 is stated in SYS-SUP-009; this item states only the latch reaction to that detection.

items.text: While no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the supervisor shall service the independent watchdog so that the time from the reset to the first service and the time between any two consecutive services are each less than 100 ms.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r1-008. STK-SUP-005 requires the watchdogs to be serviced while supervised tasks are healthy. The independent watchdog times out after 100 ms (CON-SUP-106), so the service interval must stay below that value. Reworked for F-sys-req-set-r2-012: the obligation now also bounds the first service after the reset and requires continuing service, so no timeout occurs in healthy operation. The condition equals that of SYS-SUP-011 and is the complement of the withholding in SYS-SUP-013.

items.text: After a loss of power, the controller shall start with the safe-state latch not set and without the fault history recorded before the power loss.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r1-011. CON-SUP-110 states the latch and fault history are kept in memory that survives software and watchdog resets but not power loss; SYS-SUP-029 states the survival and this item states the loss.

items.text: While the safe state is latched, including throughout every watchdog reset and software reset, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r2-011. SYS-SUP-013 withholds watchdog service while the safe state is latched, so SYS-SUP-010 and SYS-SUP-012 end in resets; CON-SUP-110 keeps the safe state latched until power-on reset. This item states that the outputs and status signal stay low during and after each such reset, not only under the start-up hold of SYS-SUP-020, which ends when the start-up checks pass.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected and the safe state is not latched, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low from the instant of safe-state entry until the reset that follows.
items.rationale: Added for F-sys-req-set-r3-011. SYS-SUP-022 drives the outputs and status low within 50 ms; SYS-SUP-046 holds them only while the safe state is latched; SYS-SUP-020 holds them from the reset until the start-up checks pass. This item closes the gap in between for an unlatched fault: low from entry until the reset requested under SYS-SUP-027.

open_points.text: The count at which the safe state latches is ambiguous in CON-SUP-110: it is not decided whether the safe state is kept at the third detection of the same fault code (no third reset requested) or after the third supervisor reset (at the fourth detection). The latch point is needed.

STK-SUP-011 and CON-SUP-111 require the reset cause to be readable by the service tool, but CON-SUP-113 defines no request or response field that returns it (GET STATUS returns only state and fault count, any other request is answered ERR). The way the service tool reads the reset cause is needed.
The entity field of the fault report is not defined for fault code 8 (watchdog reset) and fault code 9 (configuration out of range) in CON-SUP-112. The entity values for these two codes are needed.

The stored reference for the program-code check (location, algorithm, and whether run-time checking compares per segment or per full pass) is not given; CON-SUP-107 fixes only the address range and the configuration CRC. The system requirements are verifiable as a mismatch against a stored reference.
The values of <state> in STS, the meaning of <fault count> (since power-on or since reset), the request framing and the start-up message format are not given in CON-SUP-111 and CON-SUP-113.
The origin of <ms since start> in the fault report (last reset or power-on) and its behaviour on counter wrap is not given in CON-SUP-112.
The configured core clock value used for the processor-time measurement of CON-SUP-114 is not given.

For SYS-SUP-003 and SYS-SUP-004, the handling of a start (SYS-SUP-003) or completion (SYS-SUP-004) that falls in the same 100 µs measurement step as the expiry of the late-start or execution limit is not given in CON-SUP-103, nor is how elapsed time is quantized. SYS-SUP-004 detects at the expiry instant of CON-SUP-105 and SYS-SUP-003 is verifiable for starts before and after the limit; the coincident step is a measurement detail.

CON-SUP-103 defines a late start as a start later than the limit but does not state when the late-start fault is detected for a task that has not started at all (at expiry of the limit, or only when a start occurs). SYS-SUP-003 is verifiable for a task that starts late; the detection instant for a never-started task, and so the reference of the 50 ms reaction of SYS-SUP-022, is a timing detail to settle with the scheduler design.

CON-SUP-110 requires the fault report to be transmitted after entering the safe state, CON-SUP-112 requires it within 10 ms of detection, and SYS-SUP-022 (from CON-SUP-105) allows up to 50 ms from the detectable instant to safe-state entry. These cannot all hold unless safe-state entry is within 10 ms. A decision is needed: (a) transmit after entry and shorten entry to 10 ms or less, (b) keep the 50 ms entry time and read the 10 ms as not binding after entry, or (c) allow transmission before or during entry. It also affects SYS-SUP-027.
